lots.working: AS IS means untested or possibly faulty, so the similar-condition SOLD comparable is the untested unit at US$71.34 = A$102 (rate 1.428). Keep: 102 / 1.198 = 85.1, so $85. Boxed tested units (A$302-645) are not the same condition. Flip: likely as-is boxed resale about A$180 (untested unit A$102 plus box value; the PriceCharting box-only guide is US$71), less 12% eBay fees (A$22) and A$20 postage = A$138; 138 / 2.396 = 57.6, so $55. If Gowans confirms it powers on and plays, boxed sales of A$300+ would support more.
lots.confidence_reason: Box label read clearly and several SOLD pages opened, but the AS IS condition matches only one sale (untested, unboxed) and the contents are unseen.

lots.working: No SOLD entry is the same item: all are genuine Edison machines, which collectors value above German copies. So no maximum bid under the rules. As a rough pointer only, genuine Edison results suggest a copy might make perhaps A$150-350, but that is inference, not evidence.

lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged photo 2: a small gold shield transfer at the base of the gear housing, below the winding crank, with stylised letters (possibly 'PUCK' or similar). It does not read EDISON, which supports the German-copy title. Winding key has a stamped number and text that can't be read. Short nickel mandrel, reproducer carriage on a feed screw, brass ball governor, aluminium horn, bentwood oak cover with handle. Cylinders: Edison Record 13783 Harry Lauder 'He Was Very Kind to Me', 10347 (Albert Whelan waltz), and one numbered 83, all in worn original tubes.
lots.condition: Japanning glossy with some wear. Mechanism looks complete with one head shown, and Gowans says the second head is in the office. Horn sound. Cover fine. Untested. 1 bid already.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please read the maker's name on the small gold shield under the crank and on the winding key. Does the motor wind and turn the mandrel? Are both heads (playing and recording) complete, with diaphragms intact? Does the horn fit the machine?
